description: Gear ratios, pulley systems and mechanical advantage calculations with worked examples.
content_html:
Why Use Gears and Pulleys?

Gears and pulleys are power-transmission components — they carry force and motion from one shaft or point to another. They are also force multipliers: by choosing the right gear ratio or pulley arrangement, engineers can increase or reduce force, speed and torque to match what the application needs. A bicycle has a small front chainring and a large rear sprocket in low gear so the rider can pedal easily uphill; in high gear the ratio reverses to allow high speed on a flat road.

Gear Trains and Gear Ratio

A gear train consists of two or more gears with interlocking teeth. The driver gear is connected to the motor or input shaft. The driven gear is connected to the output shaft. When the driver turns, its teeth push the driven gear’s teeth in the opposite direction.

The gear ratio tells you how many times the driver must rotate to turn the driven gear once:

$$\text{Gear ratio} = \frac{\text{teeth on driven gear}}{\text{teeth on driver gear}}$$

Example: a driver gear has 20 teeth and a driven gear has 60 teeth. $$\text{Gear ratio} = \frac{60}{20} = 3:1$$ This means the driver must rotate 3 times for the driven gear to complete one full turn. The driven gear turns at one-third of the speed but with three times the torque. This is a speed reducer — used when high torque is needed at low speed (e.g. a winch, a robot arm).

Key Fact

Gear ratio = driven teeth ÷ driver teeth. A ratio greater than 1 (more teeth on driven than driver) means the output turns slower but with greater torque. A ratio less than 1 means the output turns faster but with less torque. Always state which gear is the driver in your working.

A compound gear train uses intermediate shafts that each carry two gears. This lets engineers achieve very large overall gear ratios without making gears unreasonably large. A clock uses a compound gear train to step down the motor speed to one revolution per minute at the minute hand.

A chain and sprocket drive works on the same principle as a gear train but the two sprockets can be far apart. The chain transmits force without slipping (unlike a belt drive). Bicycles, motorcycles and industrial conveyors use chain-and-sprocket drives. Gear ratio is still calculated using tooth counts: driven teeth ÷ driver teeth.

Pulleys and Velocity Ratio

A pulley changes the direction of a force or transmits rotary motion between shafts using a belt. A single fixed pulley only changes direction — you pull down on the rope and the load goes up, but you still need a force equal to the load’s weight. A block and tackle uses multiple pulleys to reduce the effort needed.

For a pulley system lifting a load, the velocity ratio (VR) equals the number of rope sections supporting the movable block: $$\text{Velocity ratio} = \text{number of rope sections supporting the load}$$ With 4 rope sections, VR = 4: the effort moves 4 metres for every 1 metre the load rises. This also means the effort force needed is approximately one-quarter of the load (ignoring friction).

Mechanical Advantage

Mechanical advantage (MA) tells you how much a mechanism multiplies the input force: $$\text{MA} = \frac{\text{load}}{\text{effort}}$$ If a pulley system requires an effort of 200 N to lift a load of 800 N: $$\text{MA} = \frac{800}{200} = 4$$ An MA of 4 means the machine multiplies the input force by 4. A higher MA means less effort is needed, but the effort must be applied over a greater distance. Real machines always have an MA slightly less than the VR because friction wastes some energy.

Key Fact

Mechanical advantage (MA) = load ÷ effort. An MA greater than 1 means the machine multiplies your force — it takes less effort to move a large load. Always include units: load and effort are both in newtons (N). MA itself has no units because it is a ratio.

A bearing supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction. The two main types you need to know are plain (journal) bearings and ball (rolling) bearings. A plain bearing is a sleeve of soft metal or polymer that the shaft slides against; it relies on an oil film. A ball bearing uses small steel balls running in a hardened steel race — the rolling contact dramatically reduces friction compared with sliding contact.

In the examination, “spins” alone is insufficient to describe what a ball bearing does. You must say that it reduces friction between rotating parts, allowing the shaft to turn with less energy loss and less heat generation. Ball bearings are used in electric motors, wheel hubs, gearboxes and any mechanism where a shaft must rotate at speed for extended periods.

Worked Calculation: Gear Ratio

Bramford Drives Ltd makes conveyor gearboxes for a bottling plant. The motor pinion has 18 teeth; the output gear has 72 teeth. Calculate the gear ratio.

$$\text{Gear ratio} = \frac{\text{teeth on driven}}{\text{teeth on driver}} = \frac{72}{18} = 4:1$$ The output shaft turns at one-quarter of the motor speed. If the motor runs at 1440 rpm, the conveyor shaft turns at 360 rpm with four times the torque.

Worked Calculation: Mechanical Advantage

A technician uses a block-and-tackle with 3 rope sections to lift a 600 N engine component. What effort is required (assume ideal conditions)?

Velocity ratio = 3 (three rope sections). In ideal conditions MA = VR = 3. $$\text{Effort} = \frac{\text{load}}{\text{MA}} = \frac{600}{3} = 200\text{ N}$$ In practice, friction in the pulleys means the actual effort needed would be higher than 200 N, giving a real MA slightly less than 3.
exam_tip_html: For calculation questions, always show your formula first, then substitute values with units, then give the final answer. Method marks are awarded even if your final answer is wrong. For gear ratio questions, check which gear is the driver and which is the driven — using them the wrong way round gives the reciprocal of the correct answer. For mechanical advantage, check units: load and effort must both be in newtons. MA itself has no unit. If a question asks you to “give two reasons for using a pulley”, name two distinct benefits: reduces the force needed AND changes the direction of effort — these count as separate reasons.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Gear ratio = teeth on driven gear ÷ teeth on driver gear. A ratio above 1 reduces output speed and increases torque; a ratio below 1 increases speed and reduces torque.
  • Mechanical advantage (MA) = load ÷ effort. An MA greater than 1 means the machine multiplies your input force; in a pulley system, MA equals the number of rope sections supporting the load (in ideal conditions).
  • Ball bearings reduce friction between rotating parts by replacing sliding contact with rolling contact; always state this function explicitly in exam answers rather than just writing “spins”.

practice_questions.text: A gear train has a driver gear with 24 teeth and a driven gear with 96 teeth. Calculate the gear ratio.
practice_questions.marks:
Gear ratio = driven teeth ÷ driver teeth [1 mark for correct formula]
= 96 ÷ 24 [1 mark for correct substitution]
= 4:1 [1 mark for correct answer with ratio notation]
[3 marks — method marks awarded even if arithmetic error]
Note: accept 4 or 4.0 without ratio notation for 2 marks.

practice_questions.text:
A workshop hoist uses a block-and-tackle with 5 rope sections to lift a heavy machine component weighing 1500 N.

(a) State the velocity ratio of the pulley system.
(b) Calculate the effort force required, assuming ideal (frictionless) conditions.
(c) Explain why the actual effort needed would be higher than your calculated value.
practice_questions.type: 4 marks — Calculation: Multi-Step with Unit Conversion
practice_questions.marks:
(a) Velocity ratio = 5 [1 mark]
(b) In ideal conditions MA = VR = 5
Effort = load ÷ MA = 1500 ÷ 5 = 300 N [1 mark for method, 1 mark for correct answer with unit]
(c) In a real system, friction in the pulleys and rope wastes energy, so more input force (effort) is required to move the same load / real MA is less than VR. [1 mark]
[4 marks total]

practice_questions.text: Give two distinct reasons why a pulley system is used in a vehicle engine workshop to lift an engine out of a car.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per distinct reason, up to 2 marks:
- It reduces the force (effort) needed to lift the heavy engine by multiplying the input force.
- It changes the direction of effort — the technician pulls down on the rope while the load moves upward.
- It allows a single person to lift a load that would otherwise require multiple people.
- It provides a controlled lift, reducing the risk of sudden movement.
[2 marks — must name the mechanism/benefit, not just 'easier' or 'quicker' alone]

practice_questions.text:
Norcroft Robotics Ltd designs a robotic arm. The arm joint is driven by an electric motor with a pinion gear of 15 teeth meshing with a large gear of 90 teeth. The large gear then meshes with a second pinion of 10 teeth, which drives a final output gear of 50 teeth.

Calculate the overall gear ratio of this compound gear train.
practice_questions.type: 4 marks — Calculation: Multi-Step with Unit Conversion
practice_questions.marks:
Stage 1 ratio = driven ÷ driver = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 [1 mark]
Stage 2 ratio = 50 ÷ 10 = 5 [1 mark]
Overall ratio = 6 × 5 = 30:1 [1 mark for method (multiply stages), 1 mark for correct answer]
[4 marks — method marks awarded for each stage even if overall answer wrong]

practice_questions.text: Explain why a ball bearing is used instead of a plain bearing in a high-speed electric motor shaft. Your answer should refer to the function of a ball bearing.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct point, up to 2 marks:
- A ball bearing uses rolling contact (steel balls in a hardened race) rather than sliding contact.
- Rolling contact significantly reduces friction between the rotating shaft and the housing.
- Less friction means lower energy losses as heat, longer component life, and the shaft can rotate at higher speeds without overheating.
[2 marks — answers that only say 'allows rotation' or 'spins' without mentioning friction reduction score zero]

practice_questions.text:
Harwick Elevators Ltd is designing a goods hoist for a warehouse. The engineers must choose between a chain-and-sprocket drive and a belt-and-pulley drive to transmit power from the motor to the lifting drum.

Evaluate which drive system is the better choice for this application. In your answer, consider the advantages and disadvantages of each system.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Evaluate an Engineering Decision
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7-8): Detailed comparison of chain-and-sprocket vs belt-and-pulley. Chain: no slip (positive engagement with teeth), high load capacity, suitable for heavy goods hoist, needs lubrication, noisy, more expensive. Belt: quieter, cheaper, some slip possible under high load (safety benefit in a jam but reliability concern for a hoist), no lubrication needed, can accommodate slight misalignment. Evaluates each property against the warehouse goods hoist context (heavy loads, frequent use, reliability critical). Reaches a justified conclusion with engineering reasoning.

Secure (5-6): Identifies key differences (slip vs no-slip, lubrication, cost) and links at least two to the hoist context. Some evaluation but may not cover all relevant factors.

Developing (3-4): Describes one system more fully than the other. Limited comparison. May list properties without linking to the application.

Emerging (1-2): Basic description of one drive system with minimal comparison.

[8 marks]

knowledge_checks.q: A driver gear has 20 teeth and a driven gear has 80 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
What is the mechanical advantage of a system where an effort of 50 N lifts a load of 200 N?
Gear ratio is calculated by dividing the number of teeth on the _____ gear by the number of teeth on the driver gear.
In a block-and-tackle pulley system with 4 rope sections, the velocity ratio is _____.
Match each term to its correct formula or description:
right: Number of rope sections supporting the load

flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for gear ratio?
flashcard_questions.a: Gear ratio = driven teeth ÷ driver teeth.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for mechanical advantage?
A driver gear has 10 teeth and driven gear has 50 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
What does a gear ratio of 4:1 mean for output speed?
flashcard_questions.a: The output turns at one-quarter of the input speed, with four times the torque.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a chain-and-sprocket drive used for?
flashcard_questions.a: Transmitting rotary motion between two parallel shafts that are far apart, without slipping.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the velocity ratio in a pulley block-and-tackle system?
flashcard_questions.a: The number of rope sections supporting the movable (load) block.
A component that uses steel balls in a hardened race to reduce friction between a rotating shaft and its housing.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the real MA of a pulley system less than its VR?
flashcard_questions.a: Friction in the pulleys and rope wastes energy, so more effort is needed than theory predicts.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a compound gear train?
flashcard_questions.a: A gear train where one or more shafts carry two gears, allowing large gear ratios in a compact space.

flashcard_questions.q: What does MA have no unit?
flashcard_questions.a: MA is the ratio of two forces (load and effort) both in newtons, so the units cancel.

flashcard_questions.q: A single fixed pulley — does it reduce effort needed?
flashcard_questions.a: No — a single fixed pulley only changes the direction of the effort force.

flashcard_questions.q: An effort of 100 N lifts a 400 N load. What is the MA?

glossary_terms.definition: Two or more meshing gears that transmit rotary motion and can change speed, torque or direction of rotation.
The gear connected to the power source (e.g. motor), which transmits motion to the driven gear.
The gear that receives motion from the driver gear; it is the output of the gear pair.
The ratio of the number of teeth on the driven gear to the number of teeth on the driver gear.
A gear train in which one or more shafts carry two gears, allowing large overall gear ratios in a compact space.
A chain-and-sprocket drive that transmits rotary motion between two parallel shafts; the chain engages the teeth of both sprockets.
A wheel with a grooved rim over which a rope or belt runs, used to change the direction of a force or to transmit power between shafts.
The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load; equal to the number of rope sections supporting the load in a block-and-tackle system.
The ratio of the load (output force) to the effort (input force) in a mechanism; a measure of how much a machine multiplies force.
A component that supports a rotating or sliding shaft and reduces friction between moving parts.
